justifications.clinical.clinicalOutcomes: The amplitude-based, neuroplasticity-principled approach has solid backing in the broader PD-exercise literature (Farley & Koshland, Petzinger, SPARX), but PWR!Moves-specific RCT evidence is sparse; outcomes are inferred from the borrowed evidence base.
justifications.clinical.caseloadApplicability: Parkinson's is a high-volume diagnosis in outpatient neuro and geriatric caseloads, and PWR!Moves applies across disease severity (stages I-IV) in both 1:1 and group settings.
justifications.clinical.reimbursement: PD-specific therapy bills under standard rehab codes, but the signature community/group classes typically fall outside insurance and run as cash-pay wellness.
justifications.clinical.efficiency: A short (2-day) workshop conferring a 3-year credential; the group-class model also lets one clinician serve multiple patients per session.
justifications.clinical.marketDemand: A growing PD population plus evidence-driven demand for PD-specific exercise create steady demand, though PWR! competes with the better-known LSVT BIG.
justifications.clinical.patientSatisfaction: Community group exercise for PD shows high satisfaction driven by social engagement and perceived functional gains (Combs RCT), aligning with PWR!'s group emphasis.
justifications.business.cashPayViability: PD wellness and group classes are an established cash-pay niche; PWR!'s community-program model is purpose-built for recurring out-of-pocket class revenue.
justifications.business.pricingLeverage: PD specialization supports premium positioning, tempered by competition from LSVT BIG and lower-cost boxing/exercise programs.
justifications.business.marketDifferentiation: Differentiates a clinic as a Parkinson's specialist with directory listing, though it carries less brand recognition than LSVT BIG.
justifications.business.ownerLeverage: The group-class and instructor-training structure (PWR! also certifies fitness instructors) lets the model scale beyond the owner-clinician's direct hours.
justifications.business.marketDemand: Expanding PD population and rising consumer interest in disease-specific exercise underpin solid demand for a cash-pay PWR! offering.
justifications.business.efficiency: Group delivery and a train-the-team instructor pathway make the model operationally efficient relative to 1:1-only certifications.
justifications.academicClinical.facultyRecognition: Founder Dr. Becky Farley is a credible PT-neuroscientist, but the credential carries less academic standing than LSVT BIG.
justifications.academicClinical.scholarship: The underlying PD-exercise literature is rich, but PWR!Moves-specific peer-reviewed scholarship is thin (conference abstracts, case reports).
justifications.academicClinical.teachingValue: Packages teachable, evidence-based content; amplitude training, neuroplasticity principles, PD-specific progression; that maps onto neuro PT/OT curricula.
justifications.academicClinical.evidenceDepth: Strong for the borrowed principles (neuroplasticity, high-intensity, amplitude training), shallow for the PWR!Moves protocol specifically.
justifications.academicClinical.facultyDemand: Modest, niche demand; programs more often reference LSVT BIG.
justifications.academicClinical.efficiency: Short workshop with a 3-year credential; efficient way to add PD-specific teaching content, though limited recognition caps the return.
